title: Concession, supposition and conditions that do or do not matter

constructions.label: Condition irrelevant: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not)
Only condition needed: 〜さえ〜ば (as long as)
Assumed premise: 〜としたら／とすれば／とすると (assuming that)
たとえ〜ても: even if (a hypothetical case)
いくら〜ても／どんなに〜ても: however much, however hard (a real or general case pushed to an extreme)
もしも〜なら／たら: if, by any chance
と言っても: true, but only to a limited extent
どころか: far from A (the opposite or something stronger)
ながらも: although (neutral or positive concession)
にしては: for (a standard), unexpectedly
わりに: considering the degree of A
にしても: even granting A (judgement or demand)
できれば／できたら: if possible (the speaker's wish or request)
Noun + でよければ: if this will do (a modest offer)

relationships.label: Say how a condition bears on the result: irrelevant, sufficient or assumed
Choose the adverb that matches the ending and the kind of condition
Limit a claim or reject it for something stronger
Measure a result against an expectation or grant a premise
Soften one's own wish or make a modest offer

exercises.prompt: 人数を知りたいので、パーティーに____、全員返事をください。
exercises.translation: Base: 来る（くる; come）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 全員 and the head-count purpose need replies from people who come and people who do not.
exercises.explanation: Completion: We want to know numbers, so whether or not you are coming to the party, everyone please reply. Both groups must reply, so attendance is irrelevant: 来ても + 来なくても.

options.label: 来ても来なくても
options.rationale: Completion: We want to know numbers, so whether or not you are coming to the party, everyone please reply. Both groups must reply, so attendance is irrelevant: 来ても + 来なくても.

options.label: 来さえすれば
options.rationale: 来さえすれば would make coming the one condition for replying; the speaker wants replies from everyone, including people who will not come, to count heads.

exercises.prompt:
初めての人も大歓迎です。
____、だれでも応募できます。
exercises.translation: Base: 経験がある（経験（けいけん）, experience; ある, have）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative), 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; さえ replaces が) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The first line welcomes first-timers, so experience cannot decide who may apply.
exercises.explanation: Context: First-timers are very welcome. Completion: With or without experience, anyone can apply. ある becomes あっても + なくても (the negative of ある is ない); repeating the noun (経験があっても経験がなくても) is also accepted.
acceptedAnswers: 経験があってもなくても
経験があっても無くても
けいけんがあってもなくても
経験があっても経験がなくても
経験があっても経験が無くても
けいけんがあってもけいけんがなくても

options.label: 経験があってもなくても
options.rationale: Context: First-timers are very welcome. Completion: With or without experience, anyone can apply. ある becomes あっても + なくても (the negative of ある is ない); repeating the noun (経験があっても経験がなくても) is also accepted.

options.label: 経験さえあれば
options.rationale: 経験さえあれば would make experience the requirement, which contradicts the first line welcoming first-timers.

options.label: 経験があるとしたら
options.rationale: 経験があるとしたら sets up experience as an assumed premise, but 'anyone can apply' does not follow from it, and the first line already says experience is not needed.

exercises.prompt:
試合は体育館で行います。
雨が____、予定どおり始めます。
exercises.translation: Base: 降る（ふる; fall [rain]）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: An indoor match is not affected by rain.
exercises.explanation: Context: The match is held in the gym. Completion: Whether it rains or not, we will start as scheduled. Rain makes no difference indoors.
acceptedAnswers: 降っても降らなくても
ふってもふらなくても

options.label: 降っても降らなくても
options.rationale: Context: The match is held in the gym. Completion: Whether it rains or not, we will start as scheduled. Rain makes no difference indoors.

options.label: 降りさえすれば
options.rationale: 降りさえすれば would make rain the condition for starting on time; since the match is indoors, rain decides nothing.

exercises.prompt: このレストランはいつもすいているから、____、すぐに入れますよ。
exercises.translation: Base: 予約する（よやくする; book a table）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The stated reason (always uncrowded) makes a booking irrelevant.
exercises.explanation: Completion: This restaurant is always quiet, so whether you book or not, you can get in right away. The から reason explains why booking does not matter.
acceptedAnswers: 予約してもしなくても
予約しても予約しなくても
よやくしてもしなくても
よやくしてもよやくしなくても

options.label: 予約してもしなくても
options.rationale: Completion: This restaurant is always quiet, so whether you book or not, you can get in right away. The から reason explains why booking does not matter.

options.label: 予約さえすれば
options.rationale: 予約さえすれば presents a booking as the one thing needed, but the reason given (it is always uncrowded) shows that a booking makes no difference.

exercises.prompt: かぜは、薬を____、治るまでの日数はあまり変わらないそうです。
exercises.translation: Base: 飲む（のむ; take [medicine]）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: あまり変わらない compares taking the medicine with not taking it.
exercises.explanation: Completion: They say that with a cold, the number of days until you recover hardly changes whether you take medicine or not. 'Hardly changes' only makes sense as a comparison of both cases.
acceptedAnswers: 飲んでも飲まなくても
のんでものまなくても

options.label: 飲んでも飲まなくても
options.rationale: Completion: They say that with a cold, the number of days until you recover hardly changes whether you take medicine or not. 'Hardly changes' only makes sense as a comparison of both cases.

options.label: 飲みさえすれば
options.rationale: 飲みさえすれば would make taking medicine the one condition, but 'the recovery time hardly changes' needs two cases to compare.

exercises.prompt:
財布を忘れても大丈夫です。
____、このアプリで買い物ができますから。
exercises.translation: Base: スマホがある（スマホ, smartphone; ある, have）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; さえ replaces が). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The reassurance depends on the phone the app runs on.
exercises.explanation: Context: It's fine even if you forgot your wallet. Completion: As long as you have your smartphone, you can shop with this app. The phone is the only thing needed: noun + さえ + あれば.

options.label: スマホがあってもなくても
options.rationale: スマホがあってもなくても would say the phone makes no difference, but the app runs on the phone and the reassurance depends on having it.

options.label: スマホさえあれば
options.rationale: Context: It's fine even if you forgot your wallet. Completion: As long as you have your smartphone, you can shop with this app. The phone is the only thing needed: noun + さえ + あれば.

exercises.prompt:
材料はもう混ぜてあります。
あとはオーブンで____、できあがりです。
exercises.translation: Base: 焼く（やく; bake）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative), 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: あとは marks the one remaining step before the dish is done.
exercises.explanation: Context: The ingredients are already mixed. Completion: All you have to do now is bake it in the oven, and it's done. Verb stem + さえすれば: the remaining step is enough.

options.label: 焼いても焼かなくても
options.rationale: 焼いても焼かなくても would make baking irrelevant, yet it is the step that finishes the dish.

options.label: 焼きさえすれば
options.rationale: Context: The ingredients are already mixed. Completion: All you have to do now is bake it in the oven, and it's done. Verb stem + さえすれば: the remaining step is enough.

options.label: 焼くとしたら
options.rationale: 焼くとしたら treats baking as an uncertain assumption; あとは presents it as the known last step.

exercises.prompt: 毎日少しずつ練習を____、だれでも上手になれますよ。
exercises.translation: Base: 続ける（つづける; keep doing）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The advice names the one thing that leads to improvement.
exercises.explanation: Completion: As long as you keep practising a little every day, anyone can get better. て-form + さえいれば; the verb stem + さえすれば (続けさえすれば) is equally natural and accepted.

options.label: 続けても続けなくても
options.rationale: 続けても続けなくても would say practice makes no difference to improving, which contradicts the advice.

options.label: 続けてさえいれば
options.rationale: Completion: As long as you keep practising a little every day, anyone can get better. て-form + さえいれば; the verb stem + さえすれば (続けさえすれば) is equally natural and accepted.

exercises.prompt:
通勤に時間をかけたくないんです。
家から____、給料が少し安くてもかまいません。
exercises.translation: Base: 近い（ちかい; near）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The first line makes distance from home the speaker's one priority.
exercises.explanation: Context: I don't want to spend time commuting. Completion: As long as it's close to home, I don't mind if the pay is a bit low. い-adjective く-form + さえあれば.

options.label: 近くても近くなくても
options.rationale: 近くても近くなくても would make distance irrelevant, but the first line says commuting time is what matters.

options.label: 近くさえあれば
options.rationale: Context: I don't want to spend time commuting. Completion: As long as it's close to home, I don't mind if the pay is a bit low. い-adjective く-form + さえあれば.

exercises.prompt: あの時もう少し____、試験に合格できたのに。
exercises.translation: Base: 勉強する（べんきょうする; study）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative), 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: のに regrets the one condition that was missing in the past.
exercises.explanation: Completion: If only I had studied a little more back then, I could have passed the exam. 勉強さえしていれば; 勉強さえすれば and 勉強しさえすれば are also accepted.
acceptedAnswers: べんきょうさえしていれば
べんきょうさえすれば
べんきょうしさえすれば
べんきょうしてさえいれば

options.label: 勉強してもしなくても
options.rationale: 勉強してもしなくても would mean studying made no difference, but のに regrets that the speaker did not study enough.

options.label: 勉強さえしていれば
options.rationale: Completion: If only I had studied a little more back then, I could have passed the exam. 勉強さえしていれば; 勉強さえすれば and 勉強しさえすれば are also accepted.

options.label: 勉強するとしたら
options.rationale: 勉強するとしたら sets up an open assumption about the future; あの時 and のに look back at a missed chance.

exercises.prompt: もし来年____、どの国がいいと思いますか。
exercises.translation: Base: 留学する（りゅうがくする; study abroad）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative), 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The question asks for a choice inside a situation that is only assumed (もし).
exercises.explanation: Completion: Supposing you studied abroad next year, which country do you think would be good? としたら and とすれば are accepted; とすると sounds unnatural before a question or a preference.
acceptedAnswers: りゅうがくするとしたら
りゅうがくするとすれば

options.label: 留学してもしなくても
options.rationale: 留学してもしなくても would make studying abroad irrelevant, but choosing a country only makes sense if the stay is assumed.

options.label: 留学さえすれば
options.rationale: 留学さえすれば would name a sufficient condition; the question asks for a choice within an assumed situation.

options.label: 留学するとしたら
options.rationale: Completion: Supposing you studied abroad next year, which country do you think would be good? としたら and とすれば are accepted; とすると sounds unnatural before a question or a preference.

exercises.prompt:
田中さんはもう家にいないようだ。
八時に____、今ごろは空港に着いているはずだ。
exercises.translation: Base: 出かけた（でかけた; went out）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative), 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: はずだ draws a conclusion from a departure time the speaker can only assume.
exercises.explanation: Context: Tanaka-san seems to have left home already. Completion: Assuming he left at eight, he should be at the airport by now. The past tense of the base is kept; としたら, とすれば and とすると are all accepted.

options.label: 出かけても出かけなくても
options.rationale: 出かけても出かけなくても would make his leaving irrelevant, but where he is now depends on it.

options.label: 出かけさえすれば
options.rationale: 出かけさえすれば names a sufficient condition; はずだ here draws a conclusion from an assumed fact.

options.label: 出かけたとすると
options.rationale: Context: Tanaka-san seems to have left home already. Completion: Assuming he left at eight, he should be at the airport by now. The past tense of the base is kept; としたら, とすれば and とすると are all accepted.

exercises.prompt: ホテル代が一日一万円____、一週間で七万円になる。
exercises.translation: Base: かかる（cost）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative), 〜さえ〜ば (as long as; any natural ば form) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The speaker assumes a daily rate and calculates from it.
exercises.explanation: Completion: If the hotel costs 10,000 yen a day, a week comes to 70,000 yen. としたら, とすれば and とすると are all accepted.

options.label: かかってもかからなくても
options.rationale: かかってもかからなくても would make the cost irrelevant, but the weekly total is calculated from it.

options.label: かかりさえすれば
options.rationale: かかりさえすれば would present the cost as all that is needed for some result; the sentence calculates from an assumed rate.

options.label: かかるとすると
options.rationale: Completion: If the hotel costs 10,000 yen a day, a week comes to 70,000 yen. としたら, とすれば and とすると are all accepted.

exercises.prompt: このまま雨が____、川の水があふれるかもしれない。
exercises.translation: Base: 降り続ける（ふりつづける; keep falling）. Rewrite it with one pattern: 〜ても〜なくても (whether or not; same word, affirmative and negative) or 〜としたら／〜とすれば (assuming that; 〜とすると only before a conclusion). Write only the rewritten phrase in the base's tense; recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: かもしれない predicts a risk from an assumed continuation (このまま).
exercises.explanation: Completion: If the rain keeps falling like this, the river may overflow. としたら, とすれば and とすると are all accepted.
acceptedAnswers: ふりつづけるとすると
ふりつづけるとしたら
ふりつづけるとすれば
降りつづけるとすると
降りつづけるとしたら
降りつづけるとすれば

options.label: 降り続けても降り続けなくても
options.rationale: 降り続けても降り続けなくても would make the rain irrelevant to the flood risk, which contradicts the warning.

options.label: 降り続けるとすると
options.rationale: Completion: If the rain keeps falling like this, the river may overflow. としたら, とすれば and とすると are all accepted.

exercises.prompt: ____一人になっても、この店を続けるつもりです。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: Becoming alone is a single hypothetical outcome, not a matter of degree.
exercises.explanation: Completion: Even if I end up on my own, I intend to keep this shop going. たとえ〜ても marks a hypothetical worst case that does not change the decision; もしも (もし) is also accepted with 〜ても.

options.label: たとえ
options.rationale: Completion: Even if I end up on my own, I intend to keep this shop going. たとえ〜ても marks a hypothetical worst case that does not change the decision; もしも (もし) is also accepted with 〜ても.

options.label: どんなに
options.rationale: どんなに〜ても (like いくら〜ても) stretches a degree or an amount; ending up alone is a yes-or-no event.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: もしも
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: もしも〜ても is also natural: it presents ending up alone as a possibility, while たとえ stresses that even this worst case changes nothing.

exercises.prompt: ____今回の試験に落ちても、来年また受ければいい。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 今回の pins failing to one possible event.
exercises.explanation: Completion: Even if you fail this exam, you can just take it again next year. たとえ marks a hypothetical outcome that does not change the conclusion; もしも (もし) is also accepted with 〜ても.

options.label: たとえ
options.rationale: Completion: Even if you fail this exam, you can just take it again next year. たとえ marks a hypothetical outcome that does not change the conclusion; もしも (もし) is also accepted with 〜ても.

options.label: いくら
options.rationale: いくら〜ても (like どんなに〜ても) needs an amount, a repetition or a degree; 今回の makes failing a single yes-or-no event.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: もしも
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: もしも〜ても is also natural: it presents failing this exam as a possibility, while たとえ stresses that even this worst case changes nothing.

exercises.prompt: ____少しでもいいから、毎日練習してください。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: でもいいから sets the smallest acceptable amount.
exercises.explanation: Completion: Even if it's only a little, please practise every day. たとえ〜でもいい sets a minimum that is still acceptable.

options.label: たとえ
options.rationale: Completion: Even if it's only a little, please practise every day. たとえ〜でもいい sets a minimum that is still acceptable.

options.label: いくら
options.rationale: いくら (like どんなに) pushes an amount or a degree to an extreme and says the result still holds; 少しでもいいから instead sets the smallest acceptable amount.

options.label: もしも
options.rationale: もしも introduces a case that may or may not happen; 少しでもいいから sets an acceptable minimum, which もしも does not express.

exercises.prompt: ____だれも来なくても、パーティーは予定どおり始めます。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: A negative, all-or-nothing case has no degree to stretch.
exercises.explanation: Completion: Even if nobody comes, we will start the party as planned. たとえ marks the hypothetical worst case; もしも (もし) is also accepted with 〜ても.

options.label: たとえ
options.rationale: Completion: Even if nobody comes, we will start the party as planned. たとえ marks the hypothetical worst case; もしも (もし) is also accepted with 〜ても.

options.label: どんなに
options.rationale: どんなに〜ても (like いくら〜ても) needs a degree or an amount to stretch; 'nobody comes' is all or nothing.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: もしも
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: もしも〜ても is also natural: it presents nobody coming as a possibility, while たとえ stresses that even this worst case changes nothing.

exercises.prompt: ____探しても、かぎが見つからなかった。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The search really happened and was repeated (past fact).
exercises.explanation: Completion: No matter how much I looked, I couldn't find the key. A real, repeated effort takes いくら or どんなに; both are natural here.

options.label: たとえ
options.rationale: たとえ〜ても sets up a hypothetical case; 見つからなかった reports a search that really happened.

options.label: いくら
options.rationale: Completion: No matter how much I looked, I couldn't find the key. A real, repeated effort takes いくら or どんなに; both are natural here.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: どんなに
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: どんなに〜ても also fits this real, repeated search ('however hard I looked'); いくら leans to amount or repetition, どんなに to degree, and both are natural here.

exercises.prompt: 昨日は____水を飲んでも、のどがかわいていた。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 昨日 makes the drinking a real past event, and the amount is what is stretched.
exercises.explanation: Completion: Yesterday, however much water I drank, I was still thirsty. いくら stresses the amount drunk; どんなに is also natural.

options.label: たとえ
options.rationale: たとえ〜ても sets up a hypothetical case; 昨日 and かわいていた report drinking that really happened.

options.label: いくら
options.rationale: Completion: Yesterday, however much water I drank, I was still thirsty. いくら stresses the amount drunk; どんなに is also natural.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: どんなに
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: どんなに〜ても also fits a real past amount ('however much I drank'); both adverbs are natural here.

exercises.prompt: ____練習しても、あのチームには一度も勝てなかった。
exercises.translation: Insert only one adverb: たとえ (even if), いくら (however much), どんなに (however; to whatever degree) or もしも (if, by any chance). Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 一度も勝てなかった reports a real past result of sustained effort.
exercises.explanation: Completion: However hard we practised, we never once beat that team. どんなに stresses how hard; いくら is also natural.

options.label: たとえ
